newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - LASMO fired ahead by oil price.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - LASMO fired ahead by oil price.

text.p: Oil exploration and production firm LASMO Plc is expected to roughly double its 1996 profits, which are due to be released on Thursday.
Surprisingly strong oil prices last year and increased production are the likely motors behind the profit rise, analysts said.
Forecasts for net earnings range between 64 and 75 million stg, which compares with 34 million stg in 1995 when oil prices were about 20 percent lower than were last year.
The forecasts are before dividend payment on preference shares. They include special gains, which are expected to be between 20 to 25 million stg.
Most industry watchers believe LASMO will maintain its full-year dividend on its ordinary shares at 1.25 pence per share.
Besides the results, analysts will be looking for news on developments in Algeria, Italy and Pakistan, where LASMO has promising operations in their early stages.
News of drilling succes in Algeria, where LASMO is active through a venture in which it holds a 25 percent stake, gave the company's shares a boost in December.

The company is believed to be on track to meet its production target of 200,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day this year, despite initial teething problems with the Liverpool Bay project and current technical hitches at the North Sea MacCulloch field.
Operator Conoco on Thursday delayed the start of the 50,000 barrel a day MacCulloch development, in which LASMO has a 40 percent interest, until the middle of the year.
LASMO is Britain's second biggest oil exploration and production firm after Enterprise Oil. Analysts are split on which of the two they prefer as they disagree on the companies' values.
Using the same method, mostly the net asset value approach, some believe LASMO is undervalued compared with Enterprise, while other analysts argue the opposite is the case.
